title: Failed Migrate-Data Deployment with Schema Compatibility Risk
simulationLabel: Deterministic synthetic evidence based on documented SAP Commerce Cloud operational boundaries; no live environment is accessed.
brief: Release 2026.10.16-rc3 was deployed to production with migrate data. Deployment failed at 22:04 UTC. Storefront and OCC health checks fail, order ingestion is stopped, and the previous build has not been redeployed. Lead investigation and select a safe recovery.

initialState.businessImpact: Checkout and order submission unavailable; no confirmed order loss

evidence.observation: The failure occurred after the migration phase started; no automatic application rollback is recorded.

investigations.label: Query the first deployment and startup errors

events.message: System update failed: duplicate deployment table mapping for FulfillmentRoute
migrate-data phase failed; application activation aborted

evidence.warning: Synthetic log format, not a claim about private SAP internals.

investigations.label: Review OCC health, latency, and error metrics

evidence.interpretationBoundary: The outage aligns with failed activation, not heap or connection-pool pressure.

investigations.label: Review the release schema compatibility declaration

changes.change: deployment mapping rename committed in rc3

evidence.finding: The prior build does not know the new type; rc3 contains a repairable mapping conflict. Deploying an older pre-change build is not assumed safe.

investigations.label: Inspect pre-deployment backup and recovery constraints

evidence.responsibility: Restore is initiated through supported Cloud Portal workflows; direct database access is SAP Support only.

investigations.label: Reconcile orders around the failure window

evidence.finding: Two payment authorizations require reconciliation; no order records should be invented by retrying blindly.

evidence.migrationRehearsal: passed against an older schema snapshot
evidence.risk: The production-like migration and rollback evidence gate was ineffective.

actions.label: Freeze further deployments and assign incident command
actions.outcome: Change activity is frozen and ownership is explicit.
actions.consequence: Evidence remains stable while recovery options are evaluated.

actions.label: Open SAP Support incident with deployment and backup evidence
actions.consequence: Managed database assistance is available if supported self-service recovery fails.

actions.label: Deploy corrected rc4 with migrate data after lower-environment rehearsal
actions.outcome: Corrected mapping completes the migration and application activation.
actions.consequence: Services start on a schema-compatible build; transaction reconciliation is still required.

actions.label: Run health, catalog, search, cart, checkout, order, and integration acceptance checks
actions.outcome: Recovery checks pass and payment/order exceptions are queued for controlled reconciliation.
actions.consequence: Service may return to monitored operation.

stateChanges.businessImpact: Recovered; two payment exceptions under reconciliation

actions.label: Immediately deploy the previous build against the changed database
actions.outcome: The previous build fails because schema compatibility was not established.
actions.consequence: Recovery is delayed and startup errors increase; the database is not automatically restored.

stateChanges.businessImpact: Extended outage caused by unsafe rollback attempt

actions.label: Initialize the production database
actions.outcome: The simulator blocks direct execution and records a prohibited destructive decision.
actions.consequence: Initialization would erase business data and is not an available live-production recovery strategy.

actions.label: Initiate controlled pre-deployment database/media/build restore
actions.outcome: The environment is restored to the captured state using the supported workflow.
actions.consequence: Post-restore full indexing and cross-system transaction reconciliation remain mandatory.

stateChanges.businessImpact: Recovery in progress; post-backup transactions require reconciliation

sequence.prompt: Start by establishing chronology: which environment, deployment, build, commit, migration mode, start time, and failure time define this incident?
Which time-bounded, correlated log evidence would distinguish the first migration failure from later startup symptoms?
Test competing causes with metrics. Did JVM, database, dependency, or API indicators deteriorate before activation failed?
Before proposing rollback, identify which persistent changes completed and what evidence establishes old-build compatibility.
Establish backup scope, recovery ownership, and what is excluded from the recovery point.
Recovery affects external state. Establish the payment and order divergence window before selecting a retry or restore.
Your evidence is sufficient to contain change risk. Assign incident command and decide whether further deployments should remain possible.
Defend a recovery choice against schema compatibility, RPO/RTO, media and search scope, and transaction reconciliation.
A started application is not a recovered commerce service. Define independent technical and business acceptance checks.

tutor.conclusionPrompt: Prepare your conclusion: timeline, impact, cause with uncertainty, safe recovery rationale, integrity checks, escalation, and systemic prevention.
tutor.uncertainty: Simulation coaching distinguishes documented product boundaries from synthetic scenario behavior.

solution.rootCause: A conflicting custom deployment mapping caused the migrate-data phase to fail after an additive schema change had begun. The old build was not proven schema-compatible.
solution.recovery: Freeze changes, preserve evidence, correct and rehearse the mapping, deploy a schema-compatible corrected build with migrate data, verify all critical journeys, and reconcile payment/order exceptions. Use supported backup/restore with SAP Support involvement when corrected forward recovery cannot safely restore service.
